published_suppliers.claim_read:
Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I \subseteq R$ be an ideal, and let $M$ be
an $R$-module. Assume that $R$ is $I$-adically complete and that $M$ is
$I$-adically separated.

If $m_1,\dots,m_r \in M$ have images that generate $M/IM$ as an
$R/I$-module, then $m_1,\dots,m_r$ generate $M$ as an $R$-module.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field.

1. If $X\subseteq \mathbf A_k^n$ is an affine algebraic set, then its coordinate
ring $k[X]$ is a reduced affine $k$-algebra.

2. If $A$ is a reduced affine $k$-algebra, then there exist $n\ge0$ and an
affine algebraic set $X\subseteq \mathbf A_k^n$ such that
$$ A\cong k[X] $$
as $k$-algebras.

Thus affine algebraic sets correspond to reduced affine $k$-algebras at the
object level, with the morphism half deferred to the next page.

Let $X$ be a classical affine variety over an algebraically closed field $k$,
and let $\overline f\in k[X]$. The **principal open subset** determined by
$\overline f$ is
$$ D_X(\overline f):=\{x\in X:\overline f(x)\ne0\}. $$

If $f\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is any representative of $\overline f$, then
$D_X(\overline f)$ depends only on the class $\overline f$, not on the chosen
representative. Its boundary cases are
$$ D_X(0)=\varnothing \qquad\text{and}\qquad D_X(1)=X. $$

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I \subseteq R$ be an ideal, and let $M$ be
an $R$-module.

The **$I$-adic completion** of $M$ is the inverse limit
$$\widehat{M}^{\,I}:=\varprojlim_{n \ge 1} M/I^nM$$
of the quotient system
$$M/IM \leftarrow M/I^2M \leftarrow M/I^3M \leftarrow \cdots.$$

When the ideal $I$ is fixed, this module is denoted simply by $\widehat M$.

The associated **completion map** is
$$\kappa_M \colon M \to \widehat M, \qquad m \mapsto (m \bmod I^nM)_{n \ge 1}.$$

Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I \subseteq R$ be an ideal. Assume that
$R$ is $I$-adically complete. If $u \in R$ satisfies
$$ u \equiv 1 \pmod I, $$
then $u$ is a unit of $R$.

Consequently, every element of $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $R$.

Every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of classical varieties sends every constructible subset of $X$ to a constructible subset of $Y$. In particular $f(X)$ is constructible.

Work over a fixed algebraically closed field $k$, with the Axiom of Choice. Classical varieties are separated and admit finite affine covers; they may be reducible or empty unless irreducibility is specified. Irreducible means nonempty. All fibres and points below are classical closed-point fibres and points.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field.

1. The assignments
$$ X\longmapsto I(X),\qquad J\longmapsto V(J) $$
induce mutually inverse inclusion-reversing correspondences between affine
algebraic sets $X\subseteq \mathbf A_k^n$ and radical ideals
$J\subseteq k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.

2. Under this correspondence, nonempty irreducible affine algebraic sets
correspond exactly to prime ideals.

Let $U$ be open in an affine algebraic set $X$ and let $Y$ be an affine algebraic set. A set map $\phi:U\to Y$ is a morphism over $k$ if $s\circ\phi\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ for every $s\in\mathcal O_Y(Y)$. For a map whose target is an open subset of an affine algebraic set, the phrase **locally regular morphism** means a continuous map pulling regular functions on each target open back to regular functions on its inverse image. An **isomorphism** between open subsets of affine algebraic sets is a bijection for which the map and its inverse are locally regular morphisms. Continuity and this local pullback property for the affine-target definition will be established in the next lemma; they are not assumed in the affine-target test.

Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional algebra over a field and let $J=J(A)$. Then
$J$ is nilpotent, and the quotient algebra $A/J$ is semisimple.

Let $n\ge1$, let $q$ be a prime power and put $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$ with
diagonal torus $T$ and standard basis $e_1,\dots,e_n$. Recall that an ordered
partition $\gamma=(S_1,\dots,S_r)$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ defines the coordinate
parabolic $P_\gamma=L_\gamma\ltimes U_\gamma$ of $G$, and that $L_\gamma$
depends only on the unordered collection of blocks, while $P_\gamma$ and
$U_\gamma$ depend on their order
([[def-coordinate-parabolics-for-ordered-partitions]]); for a composition
$\alpha$ this is the standard parabolic $P_\alpha=L_\alpha\ltimes U_\alpha$
([[def-compositions-partial-flags-and-standard-parabolics]],
[[thm-levi-decomposition-of-standard-parabolics-in-gl-n-fq]]).

1. **Transitivity.** Let $\delta$ and $\gamma$ be ordered partitions of
   $\{1,\dots,n\}$ such that every block of $\gamma$ is a union of blocks of
   $\delta$ and
   $\operatorname{blk}_\gamma(k)\le\operatorname{blk}_\gamma(l)$ whenever
   $\operatorname{blk}_\delta(k)<\operatorname{blk}_\delta(l)$ (that is, the
   order of the blocks of $\delta$ refines the order of the blocks of
   $\gamma$), so that
   $K:=L_\delta\le L:=L_\gamma$, $P_\delta=K\ltimes U_\delta\le P_\gamma=L\ltimes U_\gamma$
   and $U_\gamma\le U_\delta$. Then $L\cap P_\delta=K\ltimes(L\cap U_\delta)$ is a
   coordinate parabolic of $L$, and there are isomorphisms of functors
   $$R_K^{G,P_\delta}\;\cong\;R_L^{G,P_\gamma}\circ R_K^{L,L\cap P_\delta}, \qquad {}^*\!R_K^{G,P_\delta}\;\cong\;{}^*\!R_K^{L,L\cap P_\delta}\circ{}^*\!R_L^{G,P_\gamma},$$
   where each $R$ and ${}^*\!R$ is taken with respect to the displayed parabolic
   ([[def-harish-chandra-induction-and-restriction-for-finite-gl-n]]).
2. **Independence of the parabolic.** Let $\gamma=(S_1,\dots,S_r)$ be an ordered
   partition with blocks $S_1,\dots,S_r$ and let $\gamma'$ be the ordered
   partition obtained by listing the same blocks in another order, so that
   $L_{\gamma'}=L_\gamma=:L$ but $P_{\gamma'}$ need not equal $P_\gamma$. Then
   over $\mathbb C$ there are isomorphisms of functors on complex $L$-modules
   $$R_L^{G,P_\gamma}\;\cong\;R_L^{G,P_{\gamma'}}, \qquad {}^*\!R_L^{G,P_\gamma}\;\cong\;{}^*\!R_L^{G,P_{\gamma'}};$$
   equivalently, $R_L^{G,P_\gamma}W\cong R_L^{G,P_{\gamma'}}W$ for every complex
   $L$-module $W$, and $X^{U_\gamma}\cong X^{U_{\gamma'}}$ as $L$-modules for
   every complex $G$-module $X$. The isomorphisms are built from a choice of
   double-coset representatives and of isomorphisms on simple $L$-modules and
   need not be canonical; all the choices are finite.

Let $n\ge1$, let $q$ be a prime power and put
$G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$ with diagonal torus $T$. Let
$\alpha=(a_1,\dots,a_r)$ and $\beta=(b_1,\dots,b_s)$ be compositions of $n$
with blocks $I_1,\dots,I_r$ and $J_1,\dots,J_s$, and let
$P_\alpha=L\ltimes U$ and $Q:=P_\beta=M\ltimes V$ be the corresponding standard
parabolics, so that $L=L_\alpha$, $U=U_\alpha$, $M=L_\beta$, $V=U_\beta$
([[def-compositions-partial-flags-and-standard-parabolics]],
[[thm-levi-decomposition-of-standard-parabolics-in-gl-n-fq]]). Let
$\mathcal R$ be any set of permutations of $S_n$, one for each
$(W_\alpha,W_\beta)$-double coset (in particular, one may take the
$(\alpha,\beta)$-block-increasing representatives)
([[lem-standard-parabolic-double-cosets-are-young-double-cosets]]), let $X$ be
a complex $M$-module, and for $\rho\in S_n$ put
$$w_\rho:=P_\rho,\qquad M_\rho:=w_\rho Mw_\rho^{-1},\qquad V_\rho:=w_\rho Vw_\rho^{-1},\qquad C_\rho:=L\cap M_\rho,\qquad A_\rho:=L\cap V_\rho,\qquad D_\rho:=U\cap M_\rho,$$
and let ${}^\rho X$ be the $M_\rho$-module with underlying vector space $X$
and action $m\cdot x:=(w_\rho^{-1}mw_\rho)\cdot x$
([[def-g-module-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Then:

1. **Indexing by double cosets.** The $(P_\alpha,Q)$-double cosets of $G$ are
   exactly the disjoint nonempty sets $P_\alpha w_\rho Q$ with
   $\rho\in\mathcal R$, and $G=\bigsqcup_{\rho\in\mathcal R}P_\alpha w_\rho Q$.
2. **Mackey formula.** There is an isomorphism of complex $L$-modules
   $${}^*\!R_L^G\bigl(R_M^GX\bigr)\;\cong\;\bigoplus_{\rho\in\mathcal R}R_{C_\rho}^L\bigl(({}^\rho X)^{D_\rho}\bigr),$$
   where $R_{C_\rho}^L$ is the Harish–Chandra induction from $C_\rho$ to $L$
   with respect to the parabolic subgroup $C_\rho\ltimes A_\rho$
   ([[def-harish-chandra-induction-and-restriction-for-finite-gl-n]]) and
   $({}^\rho X)^{D_\rho}$ is the space of $D_\rho$-invariants of ${}^\rho X$, a
   $C_\rho$-module. Moreover
   $$P_\alpha\cap M_\rho=C_\rho\ltimes D_\rho,\qquad L\cap w_\rho Qw_\rho^{-1}=C_\rho\ltimes A_\rho,$$
   so that the restriction occurring in the summand is the Harish–Chandra
   restriction from $M_\rho$ to $C_\rho$ with respect to $P_\alpha\cap M_\rho$
   and the induction is taken with respect to $L\cap w_\rho Qw_\rho^{-1}$.
3. **Coordinate parabolics.** Let $\gamma=(S_1,\dots,S_r)$ and
   $\delta=(R_1,\dots,R_s)$ be ordered partitions of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ whose
   blocks have the sizes $a_1,\dots,a_r$ and $b_1,\dots,b_s$ of $\alpha$ and
   $\beta$, and let $P_\gamma=L_\gamma\ltimes U_\gamma$,
   $P_\delta=L_\delta\ltimes U_\delta$ be the corresponding coordinate
   parabolics ([[def-coordinate-parabolics-for-ordered-partitions]]). Choose
   $\sigma,\tau\in S_n$ with $\sigma(I_i)=S_i$ and $\tau(J_j)=R_j$ for all
   $i,j$, so that $\gamma=\sigma(\alpha)$ and $\delta=\tau(\beta)$, put
   $u:=P_\sigma$, $v:=P_\tau$, regard $X$ as a complex $L_\delta$-module by
   $\ell\cdot x:=(v^{-1}\ell v)\cdot x$, and for $\rho\in\mathcal R$ put
   $\rho':=\sigma\rho\tau^{-1}$ and $w_{\rho'}:=P_{\rho'}=u\,w_\rho\,v^{-1}$.
   Then $P_\gamma=uP_\alpha u^{-1}$ and $P_\delta=vQv^{-1}$, the sets
   $P_\gamma w_{\rho'}P_\delta=u\,(P_\alpha w_\rho Q)\,v^{-1}$ are the
   $(P_\gamma,P_\delta)$-double cosets of $G$ as $\rho$ runs over $\mathcal R$,
   and claims 1 and 2 hold with $P_\alpha,Q,L,M,U,V$ replaced by
   $P_\gamma,P_\delta,L_\gamma,L_\delta,U_\gamma,U_\delta$ and with
   $\mathcal R,\rho$ replaced by the index set $\mathcal R$ with
   $\rho'=\sigma\rho\tau^{-1}$, the groups
   $$w_{\rho'}L_\delta w_{\rho'}^{-1}=uM_\rho u^{-1},\qquad w_{\rho'}U_\delta w_{\rho'}^{-1}=uV_\rho u^{-1},$$
   $$L_\gamma\cap w_{\rho'}L_\delta w_{\rho'}^{-1}=uC_\rho u^{-1},\qquad L_\gamma\cap w_{\rho'}U_\delta w_{\rho'}^{-1}=uA_\rho u^{-1},\qquad U_\gamma\cap w_{\rho'}L_\delta w_{\rho'}^{-1}=uD_\rho u^{-1},$$
   and the $uM_\rho u^{-1}$-module ${}^{\rho'}\!X$ with underlying vector space
   $X$ and action $m\cdot x:=(w_{\rho'}^{-1}mw_{\rho'})\cdot x$, the inner
   action being the $L_\delta$-action on $X$; that is,
   $${}^*\!R_{L_\gamma}^G\bigl(R_{L_\delta}^GX\bigr)\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\in\mathcal R}R_{uC_\rho u^{-1}}^{L_\gamma}\bigl(({}^{\rho'}\!X)^{uD_\rho u^{-1}}\bigr),$$
   the induction being taken with respect to the parabolic subgroup
   $u(C_\rho\ltimes A_\rho)u^{-1}$ of $L_\gamma$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $q$ be a prime power and put $G=\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$.
Let $P=L\ltimes U$ be a split parabolic subgroup of $G$ with Levi complement
$L$ and unipotent radical $U$, and let $R_L^G$ and ${}^*\!R_L^G$ be the
Harish–Chandra induction and restriction functors attached to the pair $(L,P)$
([[def-harish-chandra-induction-and-restriction-for-finite-gl-n]]); all modules
below are complex. Then $R_L^G$ is **left adjoint** to ${}^*\!R_L^G$:

1. **Natural bijection.** For every $\mathbb C$-linear $L$-module $V$ and every
   $\mathbb C$-linear $G$-module $X$ there is a bijection
   $$\operatorname{Hom}_G\!\left(R_L^G(V),X\right)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_L\!\left(V,{}^*\!R_L^G(X)\right)$$
   which is natural in $V$ and in $X$.
2. **Description.** Writing $W:=\operatorname{Inf}_L^PV$ for the inflation of
   $V$, that bijection is the composite of the Frobenius adjunction
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(\operatorname{Ind}_P^GW,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_P(W,X)$
   for the subgroup $P\le G$
   ([[thm-induction-is-left-adjoint-to-restriction-for-finite-group-modules]])
   with the map that sends a $P$-linear $\varphi:W\to X$ to its restriction
   $\varphi|_V:V\to X^U$; this restriction is $L$-linear and takes values in the
   $U$-invariants because $U$ acts trivially on $W$.
